system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The package is heavily seller-favourable. It departs from our playbook on every substantive point. Taken together, the general disclosure, the buyer-knowledge bar and the "applies to all Claims" limitation language would leave us with very little recourse for exactly the risks the Seller's own Disclosure Letter identifies. We should reject the package's framing and send a full mark-up.

---

## 1. The "STANDARD / FINAL / settled at principal level" framing

The cover note says the [STANDARD] clauses were "reviewed and cleared by both sides," are "FINAL," and need "no further scrutiny." It also says we have "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package."

**This should not change our review, for four reasons:**
- These are statements in the counterparty's draft. They are not a record of our agreement. Nothing I have shows Wattlebridge agreeing to any of these positions. Amelia Frost has given no written authority for the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks, and those are the only relevant ones.
- Every point labelled [STANDARD] is a point where the Seller departs from our playbook. The labels mark the contentious items, not the agreed ones.
- The "market context" (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge bars) is advocacy. It is not a basis for us to move.
- I have reviewed everything, labelled or not.

**Action:** State expressly in our cover email that no term is agreed until the SPA is signed. Say that Wattlebridge has not accepted the limitation package or the disclosure framework, and that the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] labels have no status. If anyone on our side did have principal-level discussions, we should check with Amelia Frost before responding. We should not assume they happened.

---

## 2. Limitation of liability package

### 2.1 General cap (cl 12.1): Seller wants 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- 20% is our conditional fallback. It can only be used with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and **none has been given**. We cannot agree to it, and we should not signal that it is within range.
- **Push back:** counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.

### 2.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2)
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Basket type | Deductible (excess only) | Tipping (first dollar once exceeded) |

These terms work together. A AUD 25k de minimis means medium-sized claims never count toward the basket. A 250k deductible basket then removes the first quarter-million of whatever is left.
- **Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, with recovery from the first dollar.

### 2.3 Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13)
- 18 months against our 24. The 18-month fallback also needs Amelia Frost's written approval, and none has been given. **Counter at 24 months.**
- **The more important point is the rider:** "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." This is a hidden override of the general regime. It would pull Title, capacity, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations, covenants and fraud into the general cap, thresholds and time limit by default. It breaches our principle of keeping these categories separate.
- **Push back:** delete it. Reverse the default: general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims, and each other category has its own regime stated expressly.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
- The Seller wants capacity and title under the general cap and time limit "for administrative simplicity." That is not a sufficient justification.
- **Playbook:** separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar. If we don't get clean title to 100% of the shares, we have lost the whole AUD 24m bargain. A 20% cap on that risk makes no sense.
- **Push back:** reject outright.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- As drafted, this would extend caps, time bars, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**.
- **Playbook:** these are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-negotiable and no one on our team can waive it.
- Courts may in any case refuse to let a party rely on contractual limitations to escape its own fraud. Non-reliance clauses may also not fully defeat statutory misleading-conduct claims. We should not depend on either. The carve-out must be express.
- **Push back:** insert an express carve-out covering the Seller and its officers, employees and advisers. Limit the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses accordingly.

---

## 3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

### 3.1 General disclosure (DL 1.1, 1.2)
- DL 1.1 discloses everything in the whole data room. DL 1.2 discloses the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." The playbook rejects both.
- Taken together, the Seller could argue that any document anywhere in DD-002 to DD-012, or any public search, qualifies every warranty.
- **Push back:** delete 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure should count only where it is specific and fair, against a particular warranty, with enough detail for us to assess the nature and scope of the matter. Data-room documents may be referenced only where specifically cross-referred.
- **DL 1.4 (no admission):** this is acceptable in principle as a non-admission. We should confirm it cannot be read as reducing the effect of the facts disclosed. For example, the Seller must not use it to deny that the Bluefen consent is needed when that is the point of the condition.
- **Timing:** the letter speaks "as at" 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November. We need an updated letter and a bring-down at Completion. New disclosures should not automatically qualify warranties given at signing.

### 3.2 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
This is the single most dangerous clause in the package. It bars any claim about a matter "of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records." That is actual knowledge, adviser knowledge and constructive knowledge combined.

The Disclosure Letter itself tells us about the missing Bluefen consent, the unpaid Riverlark facility, the open Ironquay payment, the unfunded bonuses, the DD-006 incident and the Sandbar renewals. Under 8.3, the Seller could argue that we have **no claim on any of them** because we knew. Combined with 1.1 and 1.2, the warranties would be largely empty.

- **Push back:** delete 8.3. If any knowledge qualifier remains anywhere, it must:
  - refer to the **Seller's** knowledge, through named knowledge persons, after reasonable enquiry; and
  - never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.
- We should also consider an express statement that the Buyer's investigation does not affect its rights.

---

## 4. Specific deal risks

### 4.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DL 2)
- Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. It is a material customer. The change-control consent sits at clause 11.2, with conditions at 11.3.
- The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with the condition "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." Under that wording, a consent that is still subject to unsatisfied 11.3 conditions would satisfy the condition.
- DL 2 confirms that no final consent and **no evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied** has been provided.
- **Push back:** make it a condition precedent that, before Completion:
  - an effective written consent is obtained, in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer; and
  - the Buyer receives evidence that all 11.3 conditions are satisfied.

  The condition should be waivable only by the Buyer. The endeavours obligation should be stronger than reasonable endeavours, and we should have a termination right at the long-stop date. Reasonable endeavours alone is not acceptable for a customer of this size.

### 4.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DL 3)
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with a change-control clause at 8.1 and discharge provisions at 9.2. DL 3 confirms the facility is **not repaid and no discharge is included**.
- The Seller offers "a release to be provided following Completion." On a debt-free basis, that would leave us owning a company whose lender may hold live security, and possibly a change-of-control default.
- **Push back:** require all of the following:
  - a current payout letter;
  - repayment directly from Completion funds, shown in the funds flow;
  - executed deeds of release and security discharges, including PPSR registrations, delivered **at** Completion.
- A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from the lender **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.
- We should also check whether the Riverlark security extends to the shares themselves. That links to title (see 4.8).

### 4.3 DD-005 closing bonuses and the funds flow (DL 5)
- The Seller describes AUD 420,000 in bonuses as "a matter for the Seller" but omits them from the funds flow. DL 5 confirms this.
- The bonuses are company obligations. If the funds flow says nothing, the cost passes silently to us after Completion, on top of the price.
- The disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs. We should not assume an amount, but it may be material.
- Some bonuses depend on continued employment, so they may fall due after Completion. They still need to be funded by the Seller.
- **Push back:** treat the bonuses as a specific funds-flow line item, or as Debt/Transaction Expenses deducted from price. Either way, include all on-costs those payments trigger. Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall or post-Completion payment. Reject the statement that "the funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics" until it shows both the Riverlark payout and the bonuses.

### 4.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4)
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. That figure is not independently verified either way, so we should not treat it as confirmed unpaid, or as confirmed to be the whole amount. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- The Seller's indemnity covers only "the specific SOW3 payment." It does not address the real risk: that the IP never vests and Ironquay, or a third party, asserts rights.
- **Push back:** broaden the indemnity to cover all loss from any failure of SOW3 IP to vest in the Company, including third-party claims, re-development and remediation costs. Preserve the cure: payment of outstanding SOW3 fees, verified by cleared-funds evidence, followed by a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally as a Completion deliverable. The indemnity must not be capped at AUD 180,000 or limited by the general regime.

### 4.5 DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6; DL 6)
- A download link went to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records may be involved, covering names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps. Access, scope and any notification duty are **not established**, and the investigation is preliminary.
- The Seller calls it "not expected to be material." That is an assertion, not a finding. We should not adopt it, and we should not overstate the position either. There is no confirmed breach, no confirmed harm, no confirmed notification duty and no loss figure, so we should not put forward a numeric claim.
- **Push back:** require pre-Completion covenants to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence;
  - complete the investigation promptly, including any statutory assessment of whether notification is required;
  - give us regular written updates, access and consultation rights before any notification or regulator contact.

  Ensure the matter is not disposed of by general disclosure. How liability is allocated (warranty or specific protection) remains to be negotiated as the facts develop.

### 4.6 Sandbar renewals (DL 8)
- Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each, AUD 330,000 in total. The Seller asserts they are "ordinary-course operating costs." Its own DL 8 says the disclosure does **not** state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. The Seller's position is not supported by its own disclosure.
- **Playbook:** assess the renewals, but do not classify them automatically as Debt or seek a price deduction.
- **Push back:** request the contracts, dates, approvals, termination rights and accrual treatment. The fact that there are three "related" renewals of identical amounts to be "read together" warrants a question about whether a single commitment was split, for example to stay under an approval threshold. Make sure conduct-of-business covenants require Buyer consent to further renewals before Completion. Decide on classification after diligence.

### 4.7 Tax and IP warranties
- The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are **not settled**. Both remain open.
- **Push back:** expressly reserve both. Keep them as separate categories, not subject to the general cap, thresholds or 18 months by default. That is another reason to delete the "applies to all Claims" rider. We should not suggest liability is unlimited, and we should not accept that either point is resolved.

### 4.8 Title (DL 10)
- The Seller relies only on the DD-012 register. That is an internal document supplied by the Seller, not independent proof. DL 10 itself concedes that it does not represent that we have verified title.
- **Push back:** require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. That includes:
  - an ASIC company extract and share-structure search;
  - share certificates;
  - the constitution and any shareholder agreement;
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, which should also check whether Riverlark security covers the shares;
  - board and shareholder approvals;
  - Seller capacity and authority evidence.

  Title warranties should sit in the fundamental regime (4.8 and 2.4).

### 4.9 Lower-priority items (DL 7, DL 9)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** a notification obligation, not a consent requirement. Confirm timing and include it in the completion checklist.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** a restriction on assignment, not stated to be triggered by a share sale. Have the clause checked for any change-of-control or deemed-assignment wording before we accept that characterisation.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Framing | [STANDARD]/FINAL, "settled," limit review | Reject. Nothing agreed until signing. Full mark-up. |
| 2 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m.** No authority for the fallback. |
| 3 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k deductible | **5k / 50k, first-dollar tipping** |
| 4 | General time limit | 18 months | **24 months.** No authority for the fallback. |
| 5 | "Applies to all Claims" rider | General limits by default | **Delete.** Separate regimes stated expressly. |
| 6 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | **100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge** |
| 7 | Fraud | Covered by limits/non-reliance | **Full carve-out, to the maximum extent enforceable. Not waivable.** |
| 8 | Disclosure | Whole data room plus public records | **Specific fair disclosure only.** Updated letter and bring-down. |
| 9 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket, constructive | **Delete.** Any qualifier based on named Seller persons plus reasonable enquiry. Never applies to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities. |
| 10 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, consent-on-delivery | **CP: effective consent plus evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied, before Completion.** Buyer-only waiver. |
| 11 | Riverlark | Release post-Completion | **Payout letter, direct repayment from funds, releases at Completion** |
| 12 | Bonuses | Omitted from funds flow | **Line item or deduction including on-costs, plus indemnity** |
| 13 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 indemnity | **Broaden to IP-vesting losses.** Preserve the SOW3 payment cure plus confirmatory assignment. 180k unverified. |
| 14 | DD-006 | "Not material" | **Preserve logs, investigate, update, consult.** No assumed breach or figure. |
| 15 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Diligence first.** No automatic Debt or price deduction. Check for splitting. |
| 16 | Tax/IP | "Settled" under general regime | **Reserved as OPEN.** Separate categories. |
| 17 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence** |

**Internal notes:**
- We have no authority to move to any fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-Completion Riverlark release). If the team wants that flexibility later, it needs Amelia Frost's prior written approval identifying the relevant draft. Until then, our counter should not hint at it.
- Points 5, 7, 8 and 9 are the structural core and should be resolved first. If we win the commercial numbers but lose these, our protection would be largely illusory.

I can turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up or a cover email to Seller's counsel if helpful.
=== END ADVICE ===
